steps.title: For a world fair
steps.body: For the 1855 Exposition Universelle in Paris, Napoleon III asked Bordeaux's brokers to rank the region's wines. They used prices. The red list ranked 61 châteaux, all from the Médoc except Haut-Brion in Graves, into five growths, or crus. Sauternes and Barsac were ranked separately, with Yquem on top.

steps.title: Almost unchanged
steps.body: The 1855 classification has changed only twice: Cantemerle was added soon after in 1856, and in 1973 Mouton Rothschild was promoted from Second to First Growth. The five First Growths are Lafite Rothschild, Latour, Margaux, Haut-Brion and Mouton Rothschild. Some Fifth Growths now sell for more than some Seconds.

steps.prompt: Which château was promoted to First Growth in 1973?
steps.explanation: Baron Philippe de Rothschild campaigned for decades for the promotion.

steps.title: Other rankings
steps.body: Graves has its own classification, from 1953 and 1959. Saint-Émilion's classification, from 1955, is revised about every ten years and has been controversial. Pomerol has no official classification. The Crus Bourgeois of the Médoc, re-established in 2020, rank hundreds of other estates.

steps.explanation: Pétrus, in Pomerol, was never classified; Pomerol has no classification.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The 1855 classification ranked Médoc reds and Sauternes by price
It has changed only twice, in 1856 and 1973
Graves, Saint-Émilion and the Crus Bourgeois have their own rankings
